title: Specialized Latin-1 CSV batch kernel
target: Ordinary unprojected Latin-1 batch parsing of a 256 MiB CSV buffer on Apple arm64
contract: Identical rows, fields, UTF-8 output bytes, strict/permissive behavior, chunk-boundary behavior, errors, and C ABI.
summary: Dispatches the common Latin-1 batch mode to a dedicated loop so encoding-specific state and decode operations are resolved outside the per-byte parser loop. UTF-8, projection/filter, fixed, and count modes retain the generic parser.
why_equivalent: The specialized loop preserves the generic state machine transitions and batch ownership model; focused parity tests compare Latin-1 output with the UTF-8 path across quotes, chunk boundaries, high bytes, spills, offsets, and finalization.

files.summary: Dispatches Latin-1 batches and implements the encoding-specialized parser loop.
Adds specialized-kernel parity and chunk-boundary coverage.
Adds strict modes and quote-aware complete-record benchmark boundaries.
Keeps Latin-1 as the majority while restoring representative UTF-8 PGO training.

workload: Balanced-PGO builds; 256 MiB example.csv input; ordinary Latin-1 batch; 2 warmup invocations; 12 measured samples per revision; benchmarks executed serially.
limitations: The primary proof was measured on one Apple arm64 host; x86-64 should be benchmarked independently.
The synthetic input repeats example.csv and may not represent every production column-width or quoting distribution.
Reproducing the baseline PGO number requires applying the final balanced training mix to the baseline revision.
residual_risks: The dedicated loop duplicates parser state-machine logic and therefore adds maintenance surface.
The release dynamic library grew from 57,776 to 74,544 bytes (29% at Mach-O file granularity), which may affect instruction-cache behavior on other CPUs.
Strict Latin-1 improves in release builds but its 2.25% balanced-PGO result is below the proof threshold.
notes: Broader UTF-8 and strict specializations were discarded because they regressed PGO workloads.
Latin-1 remains the majority of the PGO training mix (8 of 15 sessions).
